quotes.text: Use Terminal for data collection of NFC instruments with the reader hardware interfaces.

old_evidence.text: After tapping your NFC instrument, Stripe provides a collected data object with the NFC UID, or an error if one occurred.
You can’t use this feature to collect card payments.

findings: November identifies Terminal reader hardware collection for NFC instruments and points to iOS, Android and React Native documentation variants. The index does not contain their implementation bodies.

May documents an access request for the Collect data private preview with use case, device and integration type; offline NFC UID collection on the named S700/S710 and M2 readers; and an explicit ban on using this feature for card payments.

May documents the merchant POS initiating collection through the SDK with the UID type, a customer tapping an instrument and the SDK returning the UID in collected data or an error. That direct return differs from the separate swiped-data guide's token followed by server retrieval.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May 1, 2026 factual guide for private-preview request scope, reader models, offline support, non-payment boundary, direct UID or error and the platform-specific cancellation treatment. Preserve the dated November platform destinations as navigation.
conflicts: Source lines 19 and 28 convert dated documented reader/SDK lists into universal exclusions. Preserve the May model list and the historical iOS/Android/React Native scope; the November variant index does not settle current support for other models or integrations. The linked Terminal concept also presents historical model/preview scope without date.

The mapped cancellation rule says enabled by default on smart readers; May lists the default on supported readers in the iOS/Android prose, while disabling is described for smart readers. React Native shows an explicit disable option in an example. Preserve the supported-reader qualification and platform spellings instead of imposing a uniform default from the example.
unresolved_questions: The November variant bodies were not captured. The index cannot settle changes to availability, preview access, compatible readers, SDK defaults or behavior. It supplies no negative proof for absent variants.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/collect-nfc-data, the November 7, 2026 capture states the reader-hardware use case and routes implementers to iOS, Android and React Native; the index documents no setup, hardware compatibility, transfer result, or cancellation states (new raw lines 5-15). The May 1, 2026 capture documents a merchant requesting Collect data private-preview access with use case, device and integration type. It lists S700/S710 and M2 and offline availability, and instructs against using NFC UID collection for card payments (old raw lines 8-20). The POS app prompts through the Terminal SDK for a UID, a customer taps the instrument and the SDK returns a collected-data object with the UID or returns an error, directly to the app (old raw lines 26-50 and old raw lines 59-87 and old raw lines 93-123). May says customer cancellation is enabled by default on supported readers in the iOS and Android variants and documents a disable option for smart readers; the React Native example configures the disable option (old raw line 32 and old raw line 65 and old raw lines 104-109). source-stripe-terminal-collect-nfc-data retains the May functionality but needs date/platform scope for reader, SDK and cancellation statements.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/collect-nfc-data, retain May 1, 2026 as factual authority and add the November 7, 2026 capture to source-stripe-terminal-collect-nfc-data as a raw_reference. November's switch from full capture to platform index is navigation; missing behavior does not establish a product or availability change (new raw lines 9-15, old raw lines 22-34 and old raw lines 55-67 and old raw lines 89-99). Preserve the dated private-preview access request, named S700/S710 and M2 models, offline behavior, card-payment prohibition, and direct UID/error outcome, distinct from the separate swiped-data guide's server retrieval (new raw lines 5-15, old raw lines 8-20 and old raw line 30). Replace categorical exclusions in the mapped source with dated documented reader/variant lists and preserve the cancellation distinction: default on supported readers according to the iOS/Android prose, disable on smart readers if available, and a React Native disable example (old raw line 32 and old raw line 65 and old raw lines 104-109).
